# Three Dividend-paying Undervalued Technology Stocks to Buy


By:[Paul Dykewicz](https://www.dividendinvestor.com/author/pdykewicz-admin/)


, October 30, 2026


Link copied!


Three dividend-paying undervalued technology stocks to buy appear poised to rise toward the sky.


Investors seeking undervalued technology stocks that pay dividends can be rewarded for their patience and pursue capital appreciation from a rise in share prices, too. The advent and rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is preparing the way for further technology stock gains.


Heavy investment in data centers and AI has also triggered price increases for computer chips and the consumer electronics that use them, the[Associated Press reported](https://apnews.com/article/cpi-inflation-consumer-prices-affordability-3985019a54c82421e6112fb57baba048?user_email=05aaed36cf658406cd0fbb0afb1c187c7eb6949670826643d13ce8ce528e7b0d&utm_medium=APNews_Alerts&utm_source=Sailthru_AP&utm_campaign=NewsAlert_Oct14_2026_08:46AM&utm_term=AP%20News%20Alerts) . It helps to have the right information to choose stocks with the best prospects.


For example, the semiconductor industry’s AI investment cycle has exposed a fundamental problem: insufficient manufacturing capacity to satisfy demand, wrote Dr. Robert N. Castellano, PhD, a senior analyst with[Gilder’s Technology Report](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilders-tech-report-launch/?source=GTRGURU) and the president of[The Information Network](https://www.theinformationnet.com/about-us) consultancy. Dr. Castellano holds a Ph.D. in solid-state chemistry from Oxford University, where his thesis advisor was Nobel laureate John Goodenough. Dr. Castellano also has more than 40 years of experience analyzing high-tech and semiconductor industries, including a special focus on artificial intelligence.


*George Gilder heads[Gilder’s Technology Report](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilders-tech-report-launch/?source=GTRGURU) .*


**Three Dividend-paying Undervalued Technology Stocks to Buy: VRT**


Vertiv Holdings Co. (NYSE: VRT), a Westerville, Ohio-based global provider of critical digital infrastructure, power, thermal management, information technology (IT) and service solutions for data centers, communication networks and artificial intelligence (AI) environments, operates as a pure-play critical digital infrastructure provider. The company generates revenue by selling physical equipment, integrated solutions and high-margin lifecycle services to data centers, communication networks and industrial facilities.


The company is profiting from AI’s power and cooling requirements, Dr. Castellano told me. Vertiv, offering a modest dividend yield of 0.11%, represents one of the most attractive opportunities outside of semiconductor manufacturing because the rapid expansion of AI data centers requires increasingly sophisticated electrical power distribution, thermal management and liquid cooling systems, he added.


Santa Clara, California-based Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ: NVDA) and other chip designers introduce higher-performance processors, power consumption and heat generation per rack, creating demand for Vertiv’s infrastructure technologies, Dr. Castellano said. Unlike semiconductor suppliers, Vertiv benefits from the physical requirements of AI computing facilities regardless of which processor architecture ultimately dominates.


Chicago-based investment firm William Blair & Co. praised Vertiv’s strong second-quarter 2026 earnings growth and raised its full-year guidance on the tech company, showing that demand is translating into financial performance. Although delays in data center construction and elevated valuations present risks, Vertiv’s positioning in a critical infrastructure segment offers investors an opportunity to participate in AI growth beyond the processors themselves, the investment firm continued.

**Three Dividend-paying Undervalued Technology Stocks to Buy:** **KLAC**


KLA Corp. (NASDAQ: KLAC), headquartered in Milpitas, California, is the dominant supplier of semiconductor process-control equipment, including wafer inspection and metrology systems used in advanced logic, DRAM, HBM and advanced packaging, Dr. Castellano told me. The company’s “competitive advantage” is that increasingly complex semiconductor manufacturing requires more inspection and measurement steps to maintain acceptable yields, he added.


As competitors expand their AI-related manufacturing capabilities, KLA benefits from rising “process-control intensity,” even when overall wafer capacity grows more slowly, Dr. Castellano continued. KLA’s installed base also generates recurring service revenue, providing greater earnings stability than equipment sales alone, he added.


KLAC has been held in[Gilder’s Technology Report](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilders-tech-report-launch/?source=GTRGURU) Paradigm Pillars Portfolio since March 13, 2025. As of the close of trading on Friday, Oct. 30, KLAC has produced a 136.14% return.


“KLA’s potential undervaluation reflects the market’s tendency to treat semiconductor equipment manufacturers as highly cyclical businesses,” Dr. Castellano opined. “Investors are concerned about semiconductor capital expenditure, Chinese equipment restrictions and the possibility that AI-related investment could slow. However, KLA’s earnings opportunity is not determined solely by the number of new fabs constructed. More complicated transistors, HBM architectures and advanced packaging processes require additional inspection steps, increasing equipment spending per wafer. Consequently, a stock-price correction driven by near-term equipment concerns could underestimate KLA’s long-term earnings growth and its ability to generate substantial free cash flow.”


Citi Research values KLAC at $290 using a 38x price/earnings multiple on 2028 estimated earnings power, according to an Oct. 22 research note. The investment firm views a 38x multiple, or above a three-year average of 25x, on multiple re-ratings in the group due to growing AI wafer fab equipment (WFE) exposure.


*Chart courtesy of[www.stockcharts.com](http://www.stockcharts.com/) .*


WFE consists of specialized machinery and tools used to process silicon wafers, such as lithography, etch and deposition tools. Vendors of wafer fab equipment help to enable technological innovation, offering tools the major semiconductor customers like Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) and TSMC (NYSE: TSM) need to stay at the cutting edge in AI and electronics. AI’s integration into infrastructure is setting up a growth cycle that is projected at 8% annualized growth through 2029.


KLA Corp. also has a $200 million second U.S. headquarters in Ann Arbor, Michigan, home of the main campus of the University of Michigan. Income investors may appreciate that the company has a projected 12-month dividend yield of 0.62%, according to[www.dividendinvestor.com](https://www.dividendinvestor.com/dividend-quote/klac/) .


**Three Dividend-paying, Undervalued Technology Stocks to Buy:** **NRG**


Houston-based NRG Energy (NYSE: NRG) is an integrated electricity generation and retail energy company positioned to benefit from the rapid increase in power consumption associated with AI data centers, Dr. Castellano said. AI infrastructure requires not only advanced processors and networking equipment, but also reliable electricity supplies, making power availability an increasingly important constraint on hyperscaler expansion, he added.


NRG operates in major U.S. electricity markets, including Texas, where AI-related power demand is accelerating, Dr. Castellano said. The company has secured long-term data center electricity agreements and is investing in additional generating capacity, he added.


“These activities could provide an increasingly visible earnings stream as AI infrastructure investment expands,” Dr. Castellano said. NRG also pays a dividend, offering investors an income component alongside potential capital appreciation.


NRG’s potential undervaluation reflects investor concerns that AI-related electricity demand may not translate into the exceptionally high power prices and earnings growth previously anticipated, Dr. Castellano commented. Its shares have also been affected by broader selling in AI infrastructure companies, particularly following financing concerns surrounding CoreWeave and other heavily indebted data center developers.


Advertisement.


“However, the financial difficulties of individual AI infrastructure companies do not necessarily imply a comparable reduction in electricity consumption by established hyperscalers,” Dr. Castellano said. “NRG’s existing generating assets, retail customer base and ability to negotiate long-term electricity agreements provide advantages that newer power developers may lack. The market may therefore be discounting NRG because of speculative AI financing concerns rather than a fundamental deterioration in its long-term electricity demand outlook.”


*Chart courtesy of[www.stockcharts.com](http://www.stockcharts.com/) .*


Bryan Perry, who heads the high-income[Cash Machine](https://www.bryanperryinvesting.com/offer/cash-default/?source=GURUCASH1) investment newsletter and advisory service, helped his subscribers profit with an option recommendation in NRG that produced a 25.87% gain in his[Breakout Blue Chip Trader](https://www.bryanperryinvesting.com/offer/breakout-blue-chip-trader-web-default/?source=GURUBBCT1) service.


*Bryan Perry heads[Cash Machine](https://www.bryanperryinvesting.com/offer/cash-default/?source=GURUCASH1) .*


**Woods’ Wisdom about the Meaning of Midterm Elections**


There are key reasons for optimism in the market, especially with stocks involved in AI, said Jim Woods, who heads the *[Forecasts & Strategies](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/fs-web-default-2/?source=GURUFS)* investment newsletter, as well as the[TNT Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/tnt-trader-web-default-2/?source=GURUTNT) ,[Tactical Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/tactical-trader-web-default-offer/?source=GURUTT01) ,[Five Star Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/five-star-trader-web-default-2/?source=GURUFST) and[Bullseye Stock Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/bullseye-default/?source=GURUBEST1) advisory services that recommend both stocks and options. One reason is that a Bespoke Investment Group study of historical returns of the S&P 500 after a bull market’s four-year anniversary found that the median return in the following 12 months reached 16.8%, he added.


As far as money and investments, markets tend to be indifferent to midterm election results, Woods wrote in the November 2026 issue of *[Forecasts & Strategies](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/fs-web-default-2/?source=GURUFS)* . From a historical perspective, all the volatility usually takes place prior to the midterm elections, he added.


*Jim Woods heads[Forecasts & Strategies](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/fs-web-default-2/?source=GURUFS) and[Tactical Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/tactical-trader-web-default-offer/?source=GURUTT01) .*


“We’ve already seen that volatility so far this year, and, of course, the volatility has been exaggerated by the U.S.-Iran war, a volatile AI build-out frenzy and a Fed that’s in rate hike mode,” Woods wrote. “Yet historically speaking, midterm election years do tend to be more volatile than other years.”


For example, the average S&P 500 drawdown in midterm election years is 19%, whereas, in the other three years of the presidential cycle, it averages 12%, Woods continued. This year has been light in that respect, even with some bouts of volatility, as the S&P 500’s max drawdown sits at 9.1% dating back to Q1, he added.


“So, while volatile, this year has actually been rather calm by historical standards,” Woods wrote. “Of course, we could get an uptick in volatility in the days leading up to Election Day, but the real key is that once we do get past the midterm vote, the market tends to perform extremely well. Let’s look at a few key points of proof from the historical record, courtesy of my partners at Sevens Report Research.


Advertisement.


“First, since 1950, November is the S&P 500’s second-best performing month in midterm years, with the domestic equity benchmark up an average of 2.7% on the month while trending higher 79% of the time,” Woods reported. “Second, going back to 1974, the S&P 500 averaged a 5.7% return in the three months following midterms, and the index was positive 85% of the time,” he continued.


“Impressively, in the six months following midterm elections, the S&P 500 had an average return of 12.4%, and it was up an incredible 100% of the time,” Woods wrote. “Want more supporting evidence? Well, consider that from 1930-2026, the S&P 500 *never* declined in the 12 months following a midterm election, with an average return of 14% (considerably higher than the S&P 500’s historical average annual return of 10.5%).”


**Geopolitical Risk**


Russian forces have stepped up their attacks against Ukrainian civilians. A Russian drone struck the main railway station in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro as people waited to board a train on Thursday morning, Oct. 29, killing 15 people. 10 additional people were wounded in the strike, the latest in a series of Russian attacks on transport and energy infrastructure in Ukraine that have targeted civilians. At least 19 people, including two 15-year-old girls, were killed across the country on Thursday, Ukrainian authorities said.


Ukraine’s complaints that SpaceX had restricted its Starlink military receptors appear to have been addressed, according to the latest news reports. Its President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that the Starlink satellite internet network has been throttled down in his country to prevent stopping high-speed Russian attack drones that travel at more than 100 mph, but U.S. President Donald Trump indicated the limits had been reversed by Elon Musk, who owns the satellite system.


President Trump denied instructing the technology billionaire to restrict connectivity to Starlink’s military-grade counterpart, Starshield. Among other recent civilian deaths, a young mother and her baby girl were killed in a public park while gaining fresh air.


Russia keeps intensifying its invasion in Ukraine that has included firing on buses and other civilian targets with jet-powered attack drones. Ukraine’s capital of Kyiv has been targeted directly with women, children and other civilians dying in increased numbers. In response, more than a dozen automated turrets have been deployed around the Ukrainian capital as Russia steps up its use of faster drones that are more difficult for conventional air defenses to intercept.


Ukraine’s Air Force indicated it is using artificial intelligence and machine vision to track targets and aim through its[Sky Sentinel system](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U5muTgzi-04) to defend against the faster Russian jet-powered drones, creating a tactical battle in which warfare is moving towards machines fighting machines. The war’s escalation occurred despite recent visits to both nation’s capitals by President Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who sought to broker a peace agreement.


With military action taking place there, the Middle East and elsewhere, these three dividend-paying technology leaders offer a potential path to profitability. If investors are wary about the ups and downs of the stock market, an alternative is to trade options.
